strengths.effect: Compression completes and its temporary inode is fsynced before non-overwriting hard-link publication. A link collision cannot replace an existing committed target.
pack_existing streams original bytes in 1 MiB blocks, binds the supplied source SHA before and after packing, compares stat identity, and never moves or deletes the source.

Deterministic gzip header choices; receipts expose compressed and raw hashes and byte counts; readers require both external SHA identities and reject tested corruption, truncation and ordinary decode-time drift.

findings.title: A cleanup failure is returned as write failure after the complete target has already been committed.
findings.evidence_type: Direct control-flow inspection; not covered by the 20 executed tests and no additional injected test run.
findings.trigger: os.link(temporary,p) succeeds, then temporary.unlink() raises (for example a directory permission change or transient filesystem failure).
findings.actual_effect: The caller receives an exception and no receipt, although p exists with a complete committed artifact. Retrying then raises FileExistsError, making a successful commit look failed or resume-conflicted. Both committed target and duplicate partial can remain.
findings.expected_behavior: Treat successful hard-link publication as committed. Preserve the complete target and duplicate partial evidence, return the verified receipt, and explicitly report cleanup pending (with the partial path/error). Never delete the committed target to simulate rollback.
findings.test_expectation: Inject unlink failure only after successful link; assert complete target, retained duplicate partial, successful receipt/committed status with cleanup_pending, and unchanged original source.

findings.title: The reader exposes no inflated-byte rejection budget before whole-payload allocation.
findings.evidence_type: Direct allocation/control-flow inspection; no large-input or RSS experiment run by reviewer.
findings.trigger: A valid externally hash-bound archive has an uncompressed body larger than the available decode budget.
findings.actual_effect: gzip stream.read() inflates all bytes without a limit, after which json.loads additionally builds text/objects. Hash verification does not protect capacity. The write/pack streaming behavior therefore does not make reading memory bounded; a small compressed archive may exhaust memory before returning or rejecting. This mirrors legacy whole-JSON parsing but remains an important limitation of the new API.
findings.expected_behavior: Add an explicit caller-supplied max_uncompressed_bytes limit now, enforce it incrementally while inflating, and reject before accepting more than that raw-byte budget. Do not rely on gzip ISIZE or an untrusted size estimate. Keep both SHA checks. Document that a raw-byte bound does not bound decoded-object RSS; require measured real decode RSS for later reader/resource admission.
findings.test_expectation: Small boundary cases for exact limit and limit+1, with the latter rejecting during incremental inflate, plus existing corruption and identity checks. No production-sized test is needed to establish the rejection rule.
findings.scope_qualification: This is a Task1 API rejection contract, not an M resource approval. Streaming source-only byte packing can be profiled independently; no future H/M reader is admitted.

findings.title: Finite JSON exponent literals can silently decode into nonfinite float results.
findings.evidence_type: Static reasoning from json.loads default parse_float behavior; no extra probe/test run.
findings.trigger: An externally bound valid JSON payload contains a finite number token outside binary64 range, for example {"score":1e400}. pack_existing preserves it exactly and both hashes can legitimately match.
findings.actual_effect: parse_constant rejects NaN/Infinity tokens but does not intercept the numeric token 1e400; the default float conversion yields positive infinity. The reader silently manufactures a nonfinite scientific value despite the writer rejecting such values. Precision strings are unaffected.
findings.expected_behavior: Use a checked float parser that rejects overflow/nonfinite decoded numbers with ValueError while retaining ordinary finite float behavior and all precision strings; alternatively define an explicit exact numeric representation without silently changing established result types.
findings.test_expectation: Bound external streams containing positive/negative exponent overflow must reject; ordinary finite exponents, negative zero, integer behavior and precision strings must remain unchanged.

nonblocking_transport_notes.note: File content is fsynced, but containing-directory metadata is not fsynced after link/unlink. The tested contract establishes process-visible complete-file atomic publication; power-loss persistence of a returned pathname/receipt is not established. If durable completion is required, directory fsync must be specified and verified.

pack_existing reads source bytes three times (initial digest, compression, final digest) and scans the compressed temporary file for its digest. This is bounded-chunk copying, not a throughput/capacity proof.

Failure partials intentionally accumulate. Existing tests cover early existing-target rejection and fsync interruption, but do not establish concurrent publication races, injected hard-link failure or post-link cleanup failure. Reconciliation and space reclamation policy remain future orchestration work.
